podcast.body: This song, featured on *Saskadelvia*, is not from the *Road Apples* sessions in New Orleans, but was written around 1991. Its lyrics concern the Polytechnique Massacre of 1989. The version on *Saskadelvia* is a live recording from 2000 at the Bell Center in Montreal, performed on an anniversary of the massacre. Guitarist Rob Baker remembered the chords, but Gordon Downie had forgotten the lyrics and needed them printed from a phone provided by a fan just before the encore performance. "I think I had suggested that we do it as an encore, and Gordon was like, yeah, I don't know the words."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This unreleased track addresses the tragic events of December 6, 1989, when Marc Lépine entered Le Cold Polytechnique in Montreal with a rifle and hunting knife, shooting 27 people and killing 14 women. The Hip performed it live occasionally but never officially released it. "The track's called Montreal and it's about the events of December 6, 1989 when Marc Le Pen walked into Le Cold Polytechnique in Montreal with a rifle and a hunting knife shooting 27 people and killing 14 women."
